findings.issue: Fixed: the stricter residual-gap policy reused receipt version 1. Earlier version-1 caches with events 0/50/100 at duration 120 and unanswered_gap_windows=[] bypassed gap checking despite two remaining 50-second gaps. Receipt version 2 now invalidates those vision/CLI artifacts; a new disk-cache regression failed on both the CLI helper and model-call count before the fix.

Fixed: two cache-hit fixtures retained 50-second or 45-second residual gaps, so HEAD refused those caches and subsequent empty mock responses raised StopIteration. Complete positive fixtures retain endpoint and zero-call cache assertions; both original sparse inputs remain explicitly covered as negative cache tests, and the original one-second dedupe test is unchanged.

Fixed: the new single-window regression began with 0/30 at duration 120, below the existing timestamp-coverage threshold of 60. Its fill was consumed by timestamp repair, causing three calls. Initial 0/30/60 plus fill70 now exercises a single 60-120 window, retains the two-call assertion and checks the remaining 70-120 gap is not cached.

needs-human: the tail exemption is unbounded and also applies to the initial answer. At duration 100, events 0/1/100 hide a 99-second gap and allow immediate caching. Issue #105 explicitly exempts the 40-second 60-100 tail but does not define a maximum exemption or require a newly added endpoint; changing that policy needs an acceptance decision.

summary: Fixed stale version-1 cache reuse and the three failing offline scenarios without weakening endpoint, cache or one-second dedupe assertions; added CLI manifest/Markdown coverage. The new cache regression failed before the fix, and full Git Bash offline checks now pass: 638 Python tests plus 109 Node scenarios, 24 Python skips, exit 0. needs-human: issue #105 does not define a maximum tail-gap exemption, so that behavior is unchanged and fixed remains false.
